text: Thank you for sharing your history. Additionally, have you noticed any differences in your height compared to your peers?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of virilization (clitoromegaly), severe acne, and bone fragility, I suspect a condition related to enzyme deficiency. Were your fractures specifically associated with low-trauma events like coughing or jumping from a small height? REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone, 17-OHP; REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency). The mention of tuberculosis is incorrect; your combination of virilization at birth, severe acne, delayed menarche, and bone fragility is classic for this enzyme deficiency. Please confirm if you have had rapid growth velocity or wide-spaced fingers, which would support this diagnosis.
